Witch doctor Zalazane seized their home, so the survivors crossed the narrow waters and landed on this coast. They gathered just yards inland rather than scatter through Durotar’s hostile red wastes. There, they built Sen'jin Village. The strand looks across the surf toward the islands they still hope to reclaim.

subzone:dawning-isles.text:
Dawning Isles. Along Silverpine Forest’s eastern edge, the Dawning Isles rise from Lordamere Lake beneath the growing numbers of Vile Fin murlocs. The Plague of Undeath blighted their shores, leaving the islets rotting. The Vile Fin murlocs hold the Dawning Isles. Before the Third War, these islets rested in Lordamere Lake’s calm, clear waters. Then the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, and corruption spread through the shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, and the islands lost their former peace.

Now the Vile Fin murlocs hold the muddy shores and tangled brush. They defend their growing colonies against anyone who tries to cross the lake. Bog beasts once prowled the blighted Dawning Isles alongside the murlocs. Since the bog beasts vanished, the Vile Fin population has swelled. The murlocs now control the isles outright, making this chain of islets their stronghold on Lordamere Lake.

subzone:dead-field.text:
Dead Field. In northern Silverpine Forest, Forsaken assaults falter at Dead Field, a ruined farmstead. Rot Hide gnolls serve the Scourge there, and the banshee Nightlash drives back each attack. In northern Silverpine Forest, the ruined farmstead has stood empty since its human occupants were lost in the Third War. Rot Hide gnolls now use the plot as a base and willingly serve the Scourge. Deathstalker scouts have seen signs of a coming military buildup that threatens Forsaken supply lines and outposts.

Small Forsaken assaults on the farm have failed again and again. Whenever the gnolls are in danger, Nightlash, a wailing banshee, appears and drives the attackers back.

subzone:deadeye-shore.text:
Deadeye Shore. Along Durotar’s eastern edge, Deadeye Shore stretches east of Drygulch Ravine. Its barren sands take their name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the Bleeding Hollow chieftain, while raptors, scorpids, and feral boars roam the coast. Beneath central Durotar’s red bluffs, Deadeye Shore runs past sand and rocky outcrops shaped faintly like a skull with one empty eye socket. The coast is named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed Bleeding Hollow chieftain who fought in the First and Second Wars.

No great settlement or military outpost holds this shore. Aggressive beasts roam the sands, and Burning Blade cultists from nearby ravine hideouts have been seen prowling toward the water.

subzone:decrepit-ferry.text:
Decrepit Ferry. At Decrepit Ferry, broken docks leave Fenris Isle cut off across Lordamere Lake. The Scourge killed the ferryman and wrecked the boats, and undead and Rot Hide gnolls overrun the shore. Before the Third War, people crossed Lordamere Lake each day from this dock. Local farmers brought fresh produce to the water and sold it to the wealthy lord of Fenris Isle and his household. For a modest fee, the ferryman carried trade goods, messengers, and visiting nobles between the mainland and the keep.

Then the Scourge swept through the kingdom, and the trade ended. The ferryman was brutally killed, the boats were smashed, and the pier fell into decay. The docks are dangerous for travelers along the lake shore. With the ferry out of service, Fenris Isle sits isolated across the water. Ghouls and skeletal warriors roam the ruins, along with Rot Hide gnolls. The old crossing is now a dangerous stretch of Silverpine shoreline.

subzone:deep-elem-mine.text: Deep Elem Mine. In central Silverpine Forest, worgen hold Deep Elem Mine and its tunnels. Once worked for ore, the mine fell when Archmage Arugal's magic swept through the region and changed its miners. Deep Elem Mine once supplied ore to the living people of Lordaeron. Then Archmage Arugal unleashed his lupine curse across Silverpine Forest, and it spread through the tunnels. The laborers succumbed and became vicious worgen. They left their pickaxes behind and claimed the cavern as a lair.

subzone:drag.text: Drag. In Orgrimmar, the Drag draws traders and craftspeople between three valleys. Its shaded red-rock canyon also descends to the Cleft of Shadow. The Drag runs between Orgrimmar’s red canyon walls, filled with crafters and traders. Unlike the Valley of Strength, where soldiers muster and receive commands, this is where daily city life unfolds. High cliffs and hides shade the street. Tanning vats, alchemical cauldrons and tinkers’ gears fill it with sound and smell. Craftsmen practice their trades and teach aspiring adventurers, from leatherworkers and tailors to the goblins at Nogg’s Machine Shop. Merchant storefronts and salvage houses line the Drag beside the guarded entrance to the underground Cleft of Shadow. Honest tradesmen share the street with shamans bound for the Valley of Wisdom and practitioners of dark arts. Beneath the canyon’s dim, dusty overhangs, their paths cross.

subzone:dreadmist-den.text: Dreadmist Den. Burning Blade cultists keep their rites beneath Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens. Red haze fills the cavern they use as a shrine to demons. Dreadmist Den opens among the jagged slopes of Dreadmist Peak. Burning Blade cultists gather in its dark sanctuary, where thick crimson vapor dims the stone tunnels to red twilight. Beyond the Horde's watch on the plains below, the cult performs demonic rites and guards its blasphemous relics. It plots to spread corruption across Kalimdor.

subzone:dreadmist-peak.text: Dreadmist Peak. At Dreadmist Peak, a red haze hangs over the crags northwest of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The Burning Blade cult keeps a refuge hidden there. Red haze dims the sky above Dreadmist Peak. At the crest and in the hollows below, Burning Blade cultists shelter warlocks and toxicologists. They poison nearby water and scheme against the new powers claiming central Kalimdor.

subzone:dreamer-s-rock.text: Dreamer's Rock. At Dreamer's Rock, Naralex sleeps while the Barrens still wait for renewal. He came to restore the land through the Emerald Dream, but his communion now feeds a nightmare. At the heart of the Wailing Caverns, Naralex lies in a chamber like a night elf barrow den. He entered a deep trance to reach the underground springs and channel the Emerald Dream into the Barrens' dry soil. Dark forces seized that connection, and his nightmare now twists the chamber's wildlife. His followers became the venomous Druids of the Fang, and terrible aberrations spill into the waking world.

subzone:dry-hills.text: Dry Hills. Witchwing harpies rule the green Dry Hills above the Barrens. The Dry Hills rise along the Barrens’ northwestern edge, beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Their slopes are greener than the dry plains below, but the bluffs offer travelers little safety. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing harpies from roosts along the crags. Their raiders swoop on supply caravans traveling the northern Gold Road. Abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines rot in the brush. Witchwing harpies strike from the hills to bleed trade routes and harass nearby settlements. So the Horde keeps a standing bounty on their feathers. Their nests and roosts are heavily defended in the rocky ravines. Hecklefang hyenas prowl there, while fierce Sunscale raptors hunt across the highlands.

subzone:drygulch-ravine.text: Drygulch Ravine. Dustwind harpies prey on supply caravans at Drygulch Ravine in eastern Durotar. Reach their rocky refuge through a cave from Razorwind Canyon or by a perilous leap from above. East of Orgrimmar, Drygulch Ravine lies sheltered among Durotar's rocky crags. A cramped natural tunnel from Razorwind Canyon is the only way in at ground level. Dustwind harpies roost along the steep cliffs, where they keep their broods and pile up goods stolen from Horde supply trains on the regional trails. The Dustwind harpies are the ravine's chief danger. Their matriarchs fiercely guard eggs tucked along the high ledges. Horde scouts often send young warriors to thin the flock, recover stolen trade crates, and break the harpies' hold on the ravine.

subzone:dustwind-cave.text: Dustwind Cave. High above Razorwind Canyon, Burning Blade initiates train in Dustwind Cave, northeast of Razor Hill. The cave shelters the cult as well as its training ground in Durotar. Dustwind Cave looks down on Razorwind Canyon, close to Razor Hill and a danger to the town. Here, the Burning Blade trains recruits beyond the notice of Horde authorities. Cultists teach forbidden dark magic and demonology, preparing initiates to weaken the young orcish realm from within Durotar's borders. Those who enter Dustwind Cave risk the Burning Blade's corruptions. Cultists wield volatile dark arts, including felblood afflictions. Their work shows the cult's hold on the demonic legacy Thrall fought to banish. Clearing the cabal from the cave matters to Durotar's fragile peace.

subzone:echo-isles.text:
Echo Isles. The Darkspear seek to reclaim the Echo Isles, now held by Zalazane. They first made their home there after crossing the Great Sea with Thrall. The Darkspear made the Echo Isles their home after crossing the Great Sea with Thrall. Their peace ended when Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's naval forces invaded Durotar during Kul Tiras' attack. The trolls drove back Proudmoore's fleet, but danger rose within their own tribe.

Zalazane, one of their witch doctors, took up dark arts and enslaved the minds of his kin. Chieftain Vol'jin and the free Darkspears fled again. Across the narrow strait, they found temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village. Aggressive predators, tainted wildlife, and Zalazane's thralls now overrun the tropical islands. The rogue witch doctor uses malevolent hexes, voodoo fetishes, and ju-ju heaps to bend beasts and captive trolls to his will. Vol'jin's scouts and warriors set out often from their camp at Darkspear Strand. On these frequent sorties, they seek the remains of their fallen and a chance to strike down the mystic who stole their home.

subzone:elder-rise.text: Elder Rise. On Elder Rise, Thunder Bluff's spiritual guides and elders gather east of the central plateau. Long suspension bridges join it to the High Rise and Middle Rise. Swaying rope bridges carry you from Elder Rise to Thunder Bluff's main mesas. Tauren druids and priests teach acolytes here, guiding them in nature and spiritual devotion. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem makes his home atop the mesa. He restored druidism among the tauren and forged close ties with the Cenarion Circle. Nearby, tribal leaders meet in the Hall of Elders to discuss the needs of their young capital. Peace holds across Elder Rise, though political tension remains. Magatha Grimtotem, matriarch of the secretive and haughty Grimtotem tribe, lives in a hut between the two bridges. Cairne Bloodhoof welcomes all tauren lineages and gives them seats on the council. Yet Magatha's presence reminds the city that not every tribe shares the Bloodhoof's pacifist ideals or unquestioning alliance with the Horde.

subzone:faol-s-rest.text: Faol's Rest. In eastern Tirisfal, Faol's Rest lies southwest of the Scarlet Monastery, neglected beneath a blighted canopy. The gravesite holds the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, founder of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Now spirits who perish near the monastery rest here. Before the Third War brought ruin to Lordaeron, mourners came to Faol's Rest to honor Archbishop Alonsus Faol. He led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and founded the paladins to defend humanity. Faol died peacefully before the Scourge arrived, spared the sight of his kingdom's fall. In those days, mourners traveled the road from Capital City to leave offerings and honor their beloved patriarch. The Plague of Undeath withered Tirisfal, and the pilgrims ceased their journeys. Now the monument lies abandoned and cracked beneath the Scarlet Monastery's high bluffs. Wild brush has reclaimed the paths, and damp mist gathers around the tomb. Those who fall near the monastery or elsewhere in Tirisfal gather their spirits here before returning to the dangers around them.

subzone:far-watch-post.text:
Far Watch Post. Horde defenders guard Far Watch Post west of the Southfury River bridge. They protect the frontier and the caravans bound for Crossroads from quilboar packs and Alliance incursions. Far Watch Post guards the western foot of the bridge from Durotar into the Barrens. Beyond it, the arid savannah begins, and the post is the first sign of Horde authority. An orcish watchtower, a burrow, and siege catapults face the plains, all kept ready for trouble.

South of the main road, peons tend riding wolves for messengers or reinforcements. The post keeps the supply road to Crossroads secure. Its defenders screen travelers and turn back roaming quilboar tribes and Alliance scouts.

subzone:fenris-isle.text: Fenris Isle. On Fenris Isle, Rot Hide gnolls and a rogue Scourge necromancer hold a fortress in Lordamere Lake, off Silverpine Forest. Fenris Keep once guarded Lordaeron’s military outpost on Fenris Isle. When the Scourge swept across northern Lordaeron, the garrison was slaughtered or fled into exile. The dead claimed the island, and Rot Hide gnolls later made it their stronghold. Their crude empire now spreads across the lake’s shores. The Forsaken of Silverpine Forest watch closely, fearing the island’s entrenched inhabitants threaten their northern lands.

subzone:fenris-keep.text: Fenris Keep. On Fenris Isle, isolated in the heart of Lordamere Lake, Fenris Keep now belongs to the Scourge. Thule Ravenclaw holds the stone fortress that once sheltered Lordaeron troops.

subzone:field-of-giants.text: Field of Giants. Across the southern Barrens, great beasts graze the Field of Giants while silithids threaten the plain. The wild country stretches from Camp Taurajo to Dustwallow's marshes. The southern Gold Road crosses the Field of Giants, far from the better-defended north. Its wooden watchtowers stand largely abandoned, and great herds roam the open flats. Hunters and naturalists come to see Kalimdor's enormous beasts, but danger also waits here. Dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, while a more sinister threat has begun burrowing underground. Silithid hives have recently broken through the ground across the Field of Giants. They mark the northernmost known sighting of these ravenous creatures in Kalimdor. Their strange mounds and aggressive swarms have alarmed the Horde. Korran, a troll scout from the Crossroads, and Ruga Ragetotem, a tauren warrior at Camp Taurajo, urge adventurers to investigate the hives and learn what draws these horrors so far from the deep deserts.

subzone:forgotten-pools.text: Forgotten Pools. In the northern Barrens, the Forgotten Pools draw wildlife, Kolkar centaur, and the Horde into a struggle for water. Northwest of the Crossroads, subterranean springs feed this oasis in the dry savanna. Fresh water gathers in the Forgotten Pools. Thick reeds, palm trees, and Laden Mushrooms grow beside the parched Barrens. Plainstriders, snapjaw turtles, and zhevras come here to drink. Along the banks, Kolkar centaur guard their camp and the water from travelers. Their claims bring them into conflict with Horde travelers from the Crossroads, and all three contend for the oasis. Deviate Fish thrive in the Forgotten Pools, one of the region’s rare surface waters where they can be found. Their presence hints at deeper ties to the strange transformative energies altering the Barrens’ water table. Horde naturalists and scouts watch the waters and unusual fungi along the banks. They are wary of what may be seeping into the soil.

subzone:fray-island.text: Fray Island. Warriors gather on Fray Island, off the Merchant Coast of the Barrens. On this rocky islet, fighters from across Azeroth test their skill in a rough training ring. Off the eastern bluffs of the Barrens, Fray Island lies beyond the watchful eyes of Orgrimmar and Theramore. Warriors of every race and creed train here. Klannoc Macleod oversees the fighting arena at the island’s heart. Seasoned fighters and raw recruits meet there in brutal brawls. Despite the hostile waters around it, Fray Island’s ring follows a simple code of martial combat. At their trainers’ direction, warriors face The Affray, a grueling gauntlet against waves of challengers. The trial ends with a bout against champion Big Will. In the ring, Horde and Alliance allegiance gives way to strength and martial discipline.

subzone:gallows-end-tavern.text: Gallows' End Tavern. In Brill, Forsaken gather at Gallows' End Tavern for hospitality and fellowship. The town's principal inn offers shelter and spirits, with class mentors and trade instructors in its halls and covert interrogations below. Along Brill's road, Gallows' End Tavern gathers newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell and traveling south toward the Undercity. Though undead, they come for fellowship, trade, and refuge. Class instructors guide young warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks. Vendors and medical practitioners are here as well. Beneath the tavern's floorboards, prisoners of war are bound and guarded out of public view. Among them are a captured Scarlet Zealot and a Dwarven Mountaineer. The Forsaken hold them for interrogation and experimentation as they fight to secure their borders against zealous crusaders and Alliance scouts.

subzone:garren-s-haunt.text: Garren's Haunt. Rot Hide gnolls prowl the ruined fields of Garren's Haunt in northern Tirisfal. The Garren family farmed here until the Scourge slaughtered them and left their home to decay. Under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, Garren's Haunt fed a human family. Before the Third War, its fields gave bountiful harvests. Then the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, and the Scourge came to the farm. Garren and his kin were slaughtered. Now gray, withered fields surround a farmhouse and barn, both decaying beneath Tirisfal's gloom. Rot Hide gnolls have claimed the farm, led by the vicious Maggot Eye. Tainted by undeath, they defend their scavenged ground fiercely. They pick clean what remains and savage travelers or Forsaken patrols passing through northern Tirisfal.

subzone:gates-of-orgrimmar.text: Gates of Orgrimmar. At Orgrimmar's southern gate, timber and iron guard the opening cut into northern Durotar's red rock. Through it, the arid wastes give way to the Valley of Strength, the capital's busy commons. The gate proclaims the Horde's endurance and strength in war. Orgrimmar's main gate guards the great chasm cut into the mountains around the city. Wooden palisades rise above the entrance, braced with iron spikes and watchtowers. Travelers from Razor Hill and Durotar's scrublands find a grand welcome—and a warning to anyone who threatens the new Horde. Armed Orgrimmar Grunts patrol the approach and watch all who enter. Beyond the gate's shadowed arch, you enter the Valley of Strength, Orgrimmar's civic and martial heart. The tunnel narrows the way for envoys, merchants, and warriors, while sentries watch those who pass. Here, Warchief Thrall's dream takes shape: a secure refuge carved from the harsh desert, where the Horde's many peoples can walk together without fear.

subzone:gold-road.text:
Gold Road. Horde caravans and warriors move along the Gold Road through the Barrens. It runs from Mor'shan Rampart on the Ashenvale border, past the Crossroads, and south. The Gold Road cuts through the Barrens as a long dirt highway. Near its northern end, Mor'shan Rampart and Mor'shan Base Camp guard against night elf incursions from Ashenvale. Farther south, a road forks east to Durotar before the Gold Road reaches the Crossroads.

Beyond the settlement, the road passes local oases and the foothills near the Wailing Caverns. Its northern span ends at a dried-up riverbed, where travelers enter the more dangerous southern Barrens. Horde trade and military movements cross Kalimdor's central territories along the Gold Road. Yet danger follows its length. Quilboar tribes, centaur warbands, plainstriders, and lions threaten supply caravans and lone messengers.

The Horde spends considerable resources placing scouts and warriors along the road. Even so, travelers leaving the major outposts stay armed and alert.

subzone:golden-plains.text: Golden Plains. Across central Mulgore, the Golden Plains lie southeast of Thunder Bluff. Tauren hunt in this sunlit basin as wandering kodo herds graze. Below Thunder Bluff’s towering mesas, golden and green grasses spread across Mulgore’s wild heart. Nomadic tauren cherish these traditional hunting grounds, where wildlife thrives. Broad kodo herds roam the basin, and hunters tell stories of legendary quarry. One is the great kodo Arra'chea, wandering through the tall grass.

subzone:greymane-wall.text: Greymane Wall. At Silverpine’s southern edge, Greymane Wall bars the way into Gilneas. King Genn Greymane raised it after the Second War, and its gates remain locked to the outside world. After the Second War, King Genn Greymane turned from the Alliance, resentful of its demands, especially the taxes for the orc internment camps. He believed Gilneas had paid enough in coin and blood for troubles beyond its borders. So he withdrew the kingdom from the Alliance and ordered a vast barrier across the head of the peninsula. When the Third War brought the Plague of Undeath and desperate refugees to the wall, its gates stayed shut.

subzone:grol-dom-farm.text: Grol'dom Farm. Along the road from Durotar to the Crossroads, Grol'dom Farm raises swine in the northern Barrens. Kranal Fiss and his family work the homestead under constant harassment from aggressive quilboars. After Durotar was settled, the Horde began farming the dry Barrens at Grol'dom Farm. Kranal Fiss and his children tend the homestead and raise pigs. Razormane quilboar raiders prowl the nearby ridges, making life here lonely and rugged. Still, the farm feeds the emerging orcish nation. Kranal Fiss tends pigs at Grol'dom Farm and knows the elemental rites. He guides young shaman through their trials, so Horde initiates on the spiritual path hold the farm in quiet regard. Seekers traveling west from Orgrimmar are regularly sent here to learn how to commune with the primal spirits of fire.

subzone:grommash-hold.text: Grommash Hold. In the Valley of Wisdom, Grommash Hold commands the red cliffs as Thrall's seat. Named for Grommash Hellscream's sacrifice, it is the political heart of the new Horde. Grommash Hold rises from the cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom. Thrall receives emissaries, petitioners, and warlords in its halls. The thick stone rooms stay dim and chilly so those attending his audiences remain alert and sober. With veteran counselors such as Eitrigg, Thrall weighs the defense of Kalimdor. Racial chieftains like Vol'jin visit the hold. Outside the fortress, Mannoroth's shattered armor and horned skull hang from an ancient tree. The memorial honors Grom Hellscream, who gave his life to slay the pit lord in Ashenvale. His sacrifice freed the orcs from the demonic blood curse. The remains also warn against a return to reckless savagery.

subzone:gunther-s-retreat.text:
Gunther's Retreat. On an island in Brightwater Lake, Gunther's Retreat shelters a renegade necromancer. Gunther Arcanus broke free of the Scourge by sheer will, yet trusts no outsider and keeps undead minions near his camp. Mist hangs over Brightwater Lake, where undead sentinels guard Gunther Arcanus's lonely camp. Raised in undeath, Gunther mastered the arcane arts and tore his soul from the Lich King's grip without help.

He mistrusts everyone and believes the undead wandering Lordaeron remain puppets of the Scourge. So Gunther withdrew to the island to practice his craft in peace. His zombie sentinels attack anyone who crosses the water.

subzone:hall-of-legends.text: Hall of Legends. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength, Horde champions gather in the Hall of Legends. Behind its guarded entrance, proven officers confer over battle plans and arm themselves with weapons and armor from wars across Azeroth and beyond. Horde officers gather in the Hall of Legends, off the busy avenues of the Valley of Strength. Beyond its guarded entrance, strategists and delegates from across the faction confer over maps of contested lands and the military strength of both factions. Chieftain Earthbind of Thunder Bluff, Blood Guard Hini'wana of the Darkspear, and Advisor Willington of the Undercity are among them. Only warriors ranked Stone Guard or higher may enter and claim the arms and spoils within. The Hall of Legends keeps armories stocked with battle-tested wargear for proven Horde officers. For those climbing the military ranks, these weapons and armor mark honor, martial skill, and hard-won victory.

subzone:hall-of-the-brave.text: Hall of the Brave. Warriors gather and train in Orgrimmar's Hall of the Brave, in the Valley of Honor. The hall serves the Horde's front-line fighters, drillmasters, and battlemasters. The Hall of the Brave overlooks the Valley of Honor's waters and training rings. Veteran officers and seasoned warriors teach initiates melee combat, stances, and discipline. Training dummies and weapons line the hall. There, battlemasters organize combatants for major military engagements across Azeroth.

subzone:hidden-path.text: Hidden Path. In Durotar, young shaman climb the Hidden Path toward Spirit Rock. Its high reaches look west across the Barrens. Above the Valley of Trials, the Hidden Path climbs through red peaks and is hard to see from the canyon floor. Mentors send young shaman along it to test their awareness and discipline. Then they commune with the spirits at Spirit Rock. From the highest reaches, you can see west across the rolling savannas of the Barrens. The Hidden Path cuts through the natural defenses around the valley. A low pass leads toward Ratchet and the road to Orgrimmar. It goes around the usual canyon checkpoints. So defenders fear Alliance infiltrators could take the quiet trail to the Horde's proving grounds.

subzone:high-rise.text:
High Rise. At Thunder Bluff's summit, High Rise draws the tauren tribes to its central fire above Mulgore. You find the High Rise at Thunder Bluff's summit, where open winds sweep over Mulgore's rolling plains. Tauren gather in its open-air amphitheater around a fire pit to hear tribal announcements and witness decisions. Tents and wooden stalls house merchants, armories, and culinary trainers, including Aska's Kitchen and Mountaintop Bait & Tackle.

Massive wooden elevators connect the lower tiers to Mulgore's prairie floor, but none reaches the High Rise from the plains. To climb here, take the way up from the wind rider roost or cross a rope bridge from Elder Rise or Hunter Rise.

subzone:hunter-rise.text: Hunter Rise. Hunters and warriors gather on Hunter Rise, Thunder Bluff’s southern mesa. Its platforms give tauren hunters, trackers, skinners, and warriors room to train and prepare for battle. Rope bridges join Hunter Rise to Thunder Bluff’s neighboring bluffs. At the heart of the mesa, the Hunter's Hall is where seasoned marksmen, trackers, and warriors teach the young. Practice grounds nearby hold training dummies, weapon racks, and skinning posts. There, tauren learn to wield spear and bow and work hides. Hunter Rise’s people hunt across the plains of Mulgore and help defend Thunder Bluff and the wider Horde. Battlemasters on the rise recruit seasoned fighters for skirmishes against Alliance incursions across contested battlegrounds. When the Horde needs defenders, those sworn to protect the herd gather here.

subzone:ivar-patch.text:
Ivar Patch. Ivar Patch lies in northern Silverpine, where a ruined harvest hides what befell its farmhands. Before the Third War, Ivar's pumpkin farm was a prosperous homestead in Lordaeron. He employed lively farmhands and servants. Then the Scourge spread the Plague of Undeath across the countryside, and the farm was consumed.

Ivar, his family, and the laborers rose again as rotting, feral ghouls. They prowl the ruined soil without their minds. Unlike the Forsaken, they have no free will.

subzone:jaggedswine-farm.text: Jaggedswine Farm. South of Orgrimmar’s main gate, Jaggedswine Farm raises swine to feed the capital. Its shed, pen, and watering hole supply the nearby stronghold. Feeding Orgrimmar is hard work. Durotar’s red soil supports little farming, so hardy livestock helps feed the city’s warriors and laborers. A timber storehouse, broad wooden pen, and natural watering hole anchor the farm. Here, swine are herded, bred, and butchered to keep the Horde’s granaries supplied. Swineherds and patrolling Orgrimmar Grunts visit the farm, though dry heat can leave it looking half-tended. Wild and mature swine roam inside and beyond the enclosures, sometimes testing nearby guards. At the edge of the valley approach to the capital, the farm is an unassuming but necessary part of Durotar’s daily supply work.

subzone:kodo-rock.text: Kodo Rock. Young tauren shamans are sent to Kodo Rock on Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. The stone rises among Mulgore’s grasses and is easy to miss among the rolling hills. Kodo Rock marks the straight path from Camp Narache to Brambleblade Ravine, where hostile quilboar hold territory. Worn earth circles its base. Its shape recalls the kodo beasts that wander the grasslands, though the stone is smaller than the bluffs around Red Cloud Mesa. For tribesfolk crossing Mulgore’s windswept plains, it is a quiet landmark. Among the Shu'halo, natural formations carry spiritual weight. Young tauren shamans beginning their spiritual walk are sent to Kodo Rock for their early rites of passage. At the solitary stone, novices commune with elemental forces and honor the natural world. Then they venture into more perilous reaches of the continent.

subzone:kolkar-crag.text: Kolkar Crag. Kolkar centaur watch the southern Durotar flats from Kolkar Crag and launch raids from the gorge. Warlord Kolkanis leads them against nearby Horde settlements. Kolkar centaur hold a fortified gorge in southern Durotar. They guard its narrow passages and watch the flats for openings in orc and Darkspear holdings. From the crag, scouts and marauders probe those defenses. For young warriors training in the Valley of Trials and patrols along the southern coast, this is the nearest organized centaur threat.

subzone:lushwater-oasis.text:
Lushwater Oasis. South of the Crossroads, travelers seek water at Lushwater Oasis, one of three life-giving pools in the Barrens. Kolkar centaur threaten those who come, while anglers cast into the tainted waters for Deviate Fish. A short march south of the Crossroads, Lushwater Oasis offers palms and springs beneath the Barrens sun. Thirsty beasts gather there, but Kolkar centaur hold the banks and ambush wildlife and travelers.

The oasis marks the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. Energies from its underground passages taint the pools, where unnatural creatures and strange mutations take hold.

subzone:magic-quarter.text: Magic Quarter. In the Undercity's northeast, Forsaken spellcasters study arcane and fel arts. The Temple of the Damned anchors their work. In the Undercity's northeast, Forsaken mages keep arcane learning alive and explore darker arts. The Temple of the Damned, built by the Scourge, now serves the free-willed undead. Beneath its vaulted ceilings, mages shape magical energies while warlocks commune with demons. Their work makes the quarter a center of study and occult research in Lordaeron. Spellcasters come here to train and practice their crafts. Portal trainers keep routes open across Horde territories, while master tailors make robes and shrouds from magically infused fabrics. Dalaran keeps academic wizardry apart from forbidden magic. Forsaken practitioners study arcane and fel power in the same halls, seeking strength against their many enemies.

subzone:malden-s-orchard.text:
Malden's Orchard. Black worgs prowl Malden's Orchard in northern Silverpine Forest. Malden, the human farmer who gave it his name, fled during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Its dark evergreen trees grow wild, and a Forsaken scout was cut off from his unit in the crumbling cottage. Malden's Orchard once sent fresh fruit to Lordaeron's towns. Malden, a human farmer, tended the land before the Third War. When the Scourge swept through the kingdom, he abandoned the farm and fled the plague.

Since then, Silverpine's dark mists have closed over the orchard. Its evergreen trees go unpruned, and fruit rots on blighted boughs. Wild predators have claimed the plot.

subzone:merchant-coast.text: Merchant Coast. Along the Barrens' eastern shore, trade and piracy shape the Merchant Coast. Ratchet handles sea trade, while pirates contest the coast. Ships link central Kalimdor with the Eastern Kingdoms and Theramore along the Merchant Coast. Ratchet, the Steamwheedle Cartel's neutral port, takes cargo from anyone with coin. Southsea Freebooters haunt the sands and nearby waters. They prey on merchant ships and set up illicit operations along the beaches.

subzone:night-web-s-hollow.text:
Night Web's Hollow. In Tirisfal Glades, spiders swarm Night Web's Hollow, the abandoned gold mine northwest of Deathknell. Newly raised Forsaken enter its tunnels to cull the vermin and prove they are ready for combat. Northwest of Deathknell, Night Web's Hollow cuts into the hills. Humans once worked its gold mine before the plague swept through Lordaeron. After the kingdom fell, the shafts stood empty.

Now webs cover the rock walls, and aggressive night web spiders fill the vale and tunnels. The Forsaken send their newly raised to kill young and adult spiders, hoping to regain access to the mine's gold.

subzone:nightmare-vale.text: Nightmare Vale. In southwestern Tirisfal Glades, Nightmare Vale lies west of the Crusader's Outpost beneath twisted trees and among hungry beasts. Once a forest haven, it now lies blighted and withered. Before the Third War, songbirds and woodland game filled this valley in the Tirisfal countryside. Then the Scourge's plague blackened and rotted its plants. Ravenous darkhounds and massive vampire bats consumed the native wildlife, leaving the hollow to scavengers and beasts of prey. Ressan the Needler, an unusually large, pale vampire bat, lurks in Nightmare Vale and is known to local travelers. The vale lies between haunted wilderness and the zealous sentries at the nearby Crusader's Outpost. Unwary travelers crossing this unforgiving expanse can quickly become prey.

subzone:north-coast.text: North Coast. Fog hangs over North Coast, where blight and murlocs rule the shore. Cold sands mark Tirisfal Glades' northern edge, strewn with rotting sea life. Before the Third War, North Coast's waters and stony beaches made a peaceful northern boundary for Lordaeron. Then the Plague of Undeath swept across the continent, and its blight seeped down the bluffs to poison the coast. The waters turned cold and murky. Now giant sea creatures wash ashore and rot beneath the lingering fog. With Lordaeron shattered, the Forsaken focus on Brill and the Capital City. Along the surf, the Vile Fin tribe keeps huts and uses nearby shallows as spawning grounds. Ravenous murlocs gather there, among them Deeb and growing tadpoles. They fiercely guard the tideline against surface-dwellers.

subzone:north-tide-s-hollow.text: North Tide's Hollow. Moonrage worgen haunt North Tide's Hollow, north of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Loyal to Archmage Arugal, they stalk the coastal woods from this base. North of the Sepulcher, the Moonrage pack holds a hollow among dense trees. Archmage Arugal brought the worgen into Lordaeron through reckless sorcery. Crude shelters offer little beyond bare necessities. Still, the hollow gives the pack a foothold near Forsaken travel routes. The Moonrage worgen answer to a will from Shadowfang Keep. They are no ordinary predators of the woods. Near the western shore and Silverpine's main road, they menace Forsaken couriers and patrols crossing the region.

subzone:north-tide-s-run.text: North Tide's Run. Along Silverpine Forest’s northwestern shore, North Tide’s Run draws young tauren druids to test themselves in the sea. A half-sunken ship marks the strand. North Tide’s Run follows Silverpine Forest’s northwestern edge beside the Great Sea. Cold sand meets pounding surf, and a partly sunken ship rests tilted in the shallows near the beach. Young tauren druids follow the path of Cenarius to North Tide’s Run on pilgrimage. They dive for relics lost to the waves, testing breath and endurance as they seek the blessing of aquatic form.

subzone:olsen-s-farthing.text: Olsen's Farthing. Along Silverpine Forest's main trade road, Olsen's Farthing lies in ruin. Since the Third War, reanimated thralls have overrun its fields. Olsen's Farthing once worked the fields beside Silverpine's main trade road. Now weeds choke the farmland, and broken buildings mark the farmstead's fall. Undead thralls roam the grounds under Thule Ravenclaw's command. They serve him and raid the road, and travelers who stray too close risk slaughter.

subzone:palemane-rock.text: Palemane Rock. Palemane Rock's gnoll camp threatens tauren near Bloodhoof Village from Mulgore's western mountains. At Mulgore's western rim, open grassland meets the mountains. An encampment guards a deep cave in the mountainside. Palemane gnolls claim the cave and the foothills around it. They attack hunters, travelers, and scouts who come too close, then fight fiercely to defend their den.

subzone:pools-of-vision.text: Pools of Vision. Forsaken gather in the Pools of Vision beneath Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff. Still waters and dim caverns shelter their enclave within the tauren capital. The Pools of Vision lie beneath Spirit Rise, below Thunder Bluff’s sunlit peaks. A cave path beside the bridge to the rise leads down into the grotto. Misty waters fill its shadowed chambers, where Horde spellcasters gather apart from the open-air lodges above. Forsaken make their base within the Pools of Vision. Undead priests practice shadowed arts, and mages conjure arcane portals. Defiler emissaries seek recruits for their campaigns in the Arathi Highlands. Whether tauren skepticism or the Forsaken’s own preference for darkness brought them here, the cavern links Lordaeron’s undead with their allies in Kalimdor.

subzone:pyrewood-village.text: Pyrewood Village. Pyrewood Village lies cut off beneath Shadowfang Keep in southern Silverpine Forest. Once part of Gilneas, it was left outside the Greymane Wall, and Arugal's curse now haunts its living residents. Pyrewood was once a prosperous Gilnean settlement. After the Second War, King Genn Greymane sealed Gilneas behind the Greymane Wall, leaving Pyrewood on the far side. When the Scourge crossed Lordaeron during the Third War, the cut-off townsfolk had no one to defend them. They survived the first wave of undead, but their nightmare began when the mage Arugal took refuge in the fortress above.

subzone:ragefire-chasm-classic.text: Ragefire Chasm (Classic). Beneath Orgrimmar, Ragefire Chasm puts the city at risk as troggs break into its tunnels. Its fiery caverns also shelter a cult with plans beyond Durotar. Ragefire troggs have pushed into the volcanic tunnels beneath Orgrimmar. They rose from deep fissures and now threaten the city's foundations. Magatha Grimtotem, a tauren, tried to make peace with them, but they answered with violence. Their tunnels run beneath stone streets and fortified towers. If the creatures keep digging upward, Orgrimmar itself is at risk.

subzone:raptor-grounds.text: Raptor Grounds. In the southern Barrens, Sunscale raptors claim the Raptor Grounds, a secluded valley west of Northwatch Hold. Their tool-making cunning and hunger for bright trinkets set them apart from ordinary beasts. West of Northwatch Hold, Sunscale raptors make their home in the Raptor Grounds. They build crude shelters and fashion primitive tools. They hunt together with uncanny skill, far beyond ordinary beasts. Their hunger for shiny or unusual things sends them against passing caravans and Horde encampments. Coins, trinkets, and supplies vanish into their canyon dens.

subzone:ratchet.text:
Ratchet. Ships crowd Ratchet's eastern docks, carrying traders between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. The Steamwheedle Cartel keeps this port neutral. Ratchet offers shelter to anyone who can pay, on the dry coast between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh. After the Third War, chief engineer Gazlowe founded the port and drew smugglers, exiles, and daring traders to Kalimdor's frontier. The Steamwheedle Cartel runs the town and keeps it neutral between the Horde and the Alliance.

Ships such as The Maiden's Fancy cross the Great Sea to booty bay, carrying goods, mercenaries, and raw materials. Ratchet Bruisers watch the docks and beat anyone who starts a fight and disrupts trade. Ratchet's docks, taverns, and workshops serve a town whose dealings reach beyond trade. A secluded tower overlooks the harbor from the hills, where warlocks including Strahad Farsan and Menara Voidrender gather. While townsfolk and sailors tend to cargo and goblin engineering, the warlocks commune with demonic forces without interference. The Steamwheedle Cartel does not enforce the moral restrictions found in traditional faction capitals.

subzone:ravaged-caravan.text: Ravaged Caravan. On Stonebull Lake's northeastern shore, smoke still rises from the Ravaged Caravan. The Venture Company convoy was bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operation, but tauren defenders destroyed it. The wrecked wagons rest on a rise above Stonebull Lake, where tauren from Bloodhoof Village stopped the Venture Company. The convoy carried mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site. Tauren defenders wrecked it before it could arrive. Venture Co. survivors still guard the wagons and smoldering crates, protecting what cargo remains.

subzone:razor-hill.text: Razor Hill. At Razor Hill, young orc and troll warriors train before setting out into Durotar. The fortified barracks stand at a crossroads linking the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar. Razor Hill joins northern Durotar to the southern coast and the Barrens across the Southfury River. Stone-and-timber barracks and orcish burrows fill the settlement, founded early in Durotar's settlement. After the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde here with a false offer of an emissary summit. Rexxar went in Thrall's stead and stopped their ambush. Razor Hill is fortified now against further attacks from the coast. Veteran officers such as Gar'Thok direct Razor Hill's defenses against nearby threats. Human marines still hold Tiragarde Keep on the eastern shore, while quilboar and harpy tribes harass supply lines. Investigators such as Orgnil Soulscar track the Burning Blade cult. Its rituals and corrupted agents lurk in nearby crags, and the investigators work to stamp them out.

subzone:razor-hill-watchtower.text: Razor Hill Watchtower. Furl Scornbrow watches Durotar from the Razor Hill Watchtower. From the red stone bluffs, he keeps watch over the plains and coast, guarding the settlement below. Above Razor Hill, the watchtower looks out across the settlement and the surrounding canyons. Thick timber and iron hold the outpost firm. Durotar faces Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders across the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists in nearby crags. From the ridgeline, a lookout can spot warbands, smoke signals, and incursions before they reach the gates.

subzone:razorfen-downs-classic.text: Razorfen Downs (Classic). The Scourge now holds Razorfen Downs, the quilboar's ancestral burial ground and capital in the southern Barrens. Amnennar the Coldbringer leads its agents, who have raised the quilboar dead and threaten to spread their power across central Kalimdor. Razorfen Downs rises among the towering, petrified vines shared with nearby Razorfen Kraul. Here the boar demigod Agamaggan fell in the War of the Ancients. For generations, the thorn labyrinth served as the quilboar's sacred burial ground and seat of power, watched over by mystics of the Death's Head tribe. The quilboar hold its dense briars holy, for their divine progenitor's blood soaked them. The Scourge has broken Razorfen Downs' sanctity. Amnennar the Coldbringer, a powerful lich in the Lich King's service, subdued the Death's Head quilboar and made their ancestral resting ground an undead stronghold. Reanimated quilboar skeletons and corpses prowl the Spiral of Thorns alongside shrieking banshees. The Horde in the nearby Barrens and emissaries from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light both see this Scourge power as a grave threat to Kalimdor.

subzone:razorfen-kraul-classic.text:
Razorfen Kraul (Classic). In the southern Barrens, Razorfen Kraul is the quilboar's ancestral heartland. The crone Charlga Razorflank rules its thorn-walled maze, from which her warriors strike across the region. Ten thousand years ago, Agamaggan gave his life against the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. The colossal boar demigod's blood fell across southern Kalimdor. From each place it touched the soil, colossal thorn vines rose, thick and impenetrable.

The quilboar believe they are the Great Boar's mortal descendants. They gathered among the briars to dwell and honor his sacrifice. Razorfen Kraul is their most revered stronghold, home to warriors, beast trainers, and shamans who shape the earth.

subzone:razormane-grounds.text: Razormane Grounds. Razormane quilboar press east from the Barrens into central Durotar. Their thorn-choked camp marks the front of a long struggle with Orgrimmar's orcs. At the Southfury River, Razormane Grounds threaten travelers beneath central Durotar's red cliffs. Here the quilboar have spread farther east from the Barrens than anywhere else. Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle lead raids on nearby orc settlements and passing supply lines. Patrols leave Razor Hill and nearby outposts, yet the Razormane replenish their ranks among the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

subzone:razorwind-canyon.text: Razorwind Canyon. Dustwind harpies threaten travelers on Razorwind Canyon’s road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. The rocky gulch cuts through Durotar, making the route north toward the Horde capital dangerous. Razorwind Canyon follows the main road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Its gullies reach east into the bluffs and west toward Tor'kren Farm. Dustwind harpies roost among the rocks and attack travelers who stray too close. With the canyon so near the capital’s trade route, Durotar’s defenders must watch its gullies. Razorwind Canyon’s winding passages cut through Durotar’s red rock hills. One eastern branch runs deep into the crags, through a cavern, and into Drygulch Ravine. Harpies roost on high perches, then descend in flocks. Travelers crossing the passes can be surrounded and cut down.

subzone:red-rocks.text:
Red Rocks. In northeastern Mulgore, the honored dead rest at Red Rocks. Young braves climb there to honor their ancestors and seek their wisdom. Red Rocks rises over northeastern Mulgore, its red stone marking sacred ground for the tauren. The most valiant dead lie here beside their forebears. Among them are chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives to found and protect Thunder Bluff.

Young tauren come to these graves as part of their rites of passage. They honor the dead and listen for wisdom on the wind. Bristleback quilboar have broken the peace at Red Rocks. They came from their dens and now infest the sandstone ledges, defiling ancestral graves with filth. For the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this desecration wounds their spiritual traditions.

Shaman and lorekeepers call for aid to cleanse the crags, drive out the Bristlebacks, and restore the resting place of their dead.

subzone:rocktusk-farm.text: Rocktusk Farm. At Rocktusk Farm, swine feed Orgrimmar from just beyond the city gates in northern Durotar. Dry, stony ground makes crops hard to grow, so the farm sends meat and provisions to the capital. Rocktusk Farm raises hardy swine on Durotar’s dry, stony ground. Crops are hard to grow here, so the farm helps feed Orgrimmar’s growing population. Near the capital’s fortified perimeter, it is safer than homesteads out in the wild red canyonlands.

subzone:rogues-quarter.text:
Rogues' Quarter. In the Undercity's southeastern wing, scouts, assassins, and underworld operatives gather in Rogues' Quarter. Its craftsmen support their covert work. Survivors skilled in stealth gather deep in the Undercity's southeastern wing. Many served the Kingdom of Lordaeron in life as thieves, cutpurses, or silent blades. In death, they use stealth, poisons, and misdirection to defend the fledgling nation from the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade.

Here, operatives sharpen daggers, brew toxins, and hone their clandestine skills. Specialized trades in Rogues' Quarter help travelers survive undercover. Artisans teach leatherworking and skinning, turning raw hides into light, silent armor. Tinkers work at engineering benches, while field medics and apothecaries teach first aid. Poison vendors nearby supply lethal reagents for covert work.

subzone:rolling-plains.text: Rolling Plains. In southern Mulgore, herds graze the Rolling Plains while centaur raiders and harpies threaten travelers. From Bloodhoof Village, the Rolling Plains run south to the earthen gates of the Barrens. Prairie wolves, kodo herds, flatland cougars, and swift tallstriders roam these open ranges of the tauren homeland. Young hunters come here to prove their worth to the elders. They learn to track, wait patiently, and respect the land. Mulgore’s ring of bluffs shields much of the region, but the Rolling Plains lie open to threats from beyond it. Centaur outriders have crossed the defenses here, the only frontier where they have managed to do so. They harass travelers and hunting parties. Windfury harpies roost in the eastern crags, swooping on stray game and vulnerable nomadic camps.

subzone:royal-quarter.text:
Royal Quarter. In the Royal Quarter, Sylvanas Windrunner directs the Forsaken from her throne. Varimathras stands at her side, and Royal Dreadguards guard the seat of power beneath the Undercity. The Forsaken make their military and political decisions in the Royal Quarter, also called the Hall of the Dark Lady. Beneath the Undercity, Sylvanas Windrunner holds court in its vast chamber. She works for the survival of her free-willed undead and the destruction of the Scourge. Royal Dreadguards watch along the dais, shielding their queen from uninvited visitors and would-be assassins. Varimathras, a nathrezim, stands beside Sylvanas in the heart of the Undercity. During the civil war in the ruins of Lordaeron, he sided with her to save his own life and pledged loyalty to her cause. From the Royal Quarter, he commands deathstalkers and coordinates defenses across the realm.

His tactical skill aids the Forsaken, yet many Horde allies distrust his true allegiance because he is a demon.

subzone:scarlet-watch-post.text:
Scarlet Watch Post. In northeastern Tirisfal Glades, the rocky hills north of the Scarlet Monastery are under watch. The garrison guards the monastery’s northern flank against attack. Behind the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Watch Post watches the northern cliffs. The southern road to the gate is busy and fortified, but the rugged cliffs along Tirisfal’s northern coast offer infiltrators another way in. The Scarlet Crusade built the stone tower to guard that blind spot. It is one of several Crusader outposts scattered across Tirisfal Glades.

Captain Melrache commands a devout force of Neophytes, Vanguards, and Friars. They watch the cliffs so neither the Scourge nor the Forsaken can surprise the order from behind.

subzone:screaming-gully.text: Screaming Gully. Steam and wind make Screaming Gully howl beneath the northern Barrens, at the Wailing Caverns’ entrance. Past the entrance, wind groans through the deep fissures of Screaming Gully. Damp growth and humid mist fill the cavern, far from the dry Barrens above. Lady Anacondra, a Fanglord, watches over the acolytes of the Druids of the Fang and fierce deviate raptors. Ancient snapping turtles patrol the shallow waters below, including Kresh.

subzone:scuttle-coast.text: Scuttle Coast. Along Durotar’s eastern shore, wreckage from Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet recalls the recent naval war. Now the Horde scavenges among the sunken ships between Razor Hill and Tiragarde Keep. Sunken warships line Durotar’s eastern edge, where the shore meets the Great Sea. During Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s invasion, the Kul Tiras fleet attacked the young nation of Durotar. Fierce battles with the Horde drove many human warships onto jagged shoals, where they broke apart. Barnacled timber, broken rigging, cargo barrels, and sunken ships still mark the coast. For the encampments at Razor Hill, the wreckage recalls how close the Kul Tiran threat remains. The name Scuttle Coast may point to warships scuttled or grounded in the fighting. It may also come from crabs and makrura picking through the wreckage. Shoreline beasts and dangerous tides keep casual travelers away.

subzone:sepulcher.text:
Sepulcher. The Forsaken hold Sepulcher above Silverpine Forest’s western coast. Once a Lordaeron graveyard and crypt, it now gives the Horde a fortified refuge amid threats across the region. Sepulcher crowns the hills above Lordaeron’s western coast. Beside the western road, its old cemetery and stone crypt now belong to the Forsaken. Since the Third War, they have turned the grounds and ancient vault into a vital outpost.

Danger presses from every side. Feral worgen stalk the south, Scourge remnants wander east, and Kirin Tor wizards watch from Ambermill. For travelers crossing Silverpine, Sepulcher offers shelter, supplies, and a place of command.

subzone:sewers.text:
Sewers. In the hills west of Lordaeron's ruined palace, the Sewers open a second way into the Undercity. Bat handlers and travelers pass through the old stone channels to reach its inner rings. The Sewers once carried water away from Lordaeron's royal capital. Now Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken have folded those old channels into the Undercity's defenses. The passage opens west of the surface ruins near a Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, then slopes into the city.

Forsaken bat handlers carry riders through the cavernous passage to the Undercity's underground rings, clear of the slow cage lifts. Yet the route also skirts the fortified courtyards. Hostile infiltrators seek to exploit that weakness.

subzone:shadow-grave.text: Shadow Grave. Newly freed Forsaken awaken in Shadow Grave, above Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Above Deathknell, newly freed Forsaken awaken in Shadow Grave. They once served the Scourge without thought. In the mausoleum's vaults, they recover their free will. Undertaker Mordo watches as they rise from stone slabs and take their first steps into a world that despises them. Then they follow the footpath down to Deathknell and pledge themselves to the Banshee Queen.

subzone:shining-strand.text: Shining Strand. Along Silverpine’s eastern shore, Shining Strand runs south beside Lordamere Lake toward Alterac’s rugged foothills. Vile Fin murlocs hold settlements in its shallows, making the coast dangerous for unseasoned travelers. Shining Strand runs along Silverpine Forest’s eastern edge beside Lordamere Lake. Several aggressive Vile Fin murloc settlements line the shallows and threaten travelers on the lake road. Feral worgen roam the deep woods behind the shore.

subzone:shrine-of-the-dormant-flame.text:
Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Horde shaman climb to the Shrine of the Dormant Flame, atop Durotar’s highest peak northwest of the Valley of Trials. Telf Joolam keeps this secluded sanctuary, where initiates prove their spiritual mastery. A narrow trail climbs from the Southfury River at the Southfury Watershed’s southwestern edge. At the summit, Durotar’s red cliffs fall away beneath a wide view, and one misstep near the precipice means certain death. Telf Joolam, a solitary hermit, oversees the sacred rites here.

Orc and troll shaman come to answer the Call of Fire. At the shrine’s brazier, they kindle sleeping coals with the ember of a defeated elemental. The trial proves they can commune with fire and respect its destructive spirits.

subzone:shrine-of-the-fallen-warrior.text:
Shrine of the Fallen Warrior. At the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, Koiter watches over an orc laid to rest on a ridge west of the Crossroads. A stone plinth marked 'MK' keeps the warrior's memory beneath the Barrens sky. High on the hills northwest of the Crossroads, the shrine offers a quiet place amid the Barrens' dust and peril. Find the ridge southwest of the summit and follow its winding path to a gentle mound. A carved stone monument rests at the top, its plinth marked with the initials 'MK'.

An armored orc warrior lies before it, watched day and night by Koiter, a Spirit Healer. No battle horns sound here. The shrine honors a champion who walked Kalimdor's lands. The shrine honors a departed champion of the Horde. The warrior's soul lingers in the spirits' care, beneath the watch of Koiter.

The monument also remembers Michel Koiter, an illustrator who died while the world was being made. The resting warrior was modeled on Koiter's own early character, Twincruiser, and his memory remains beneath Kalimdor's open skies.

subzone:skittering-dark.text: Skittering Dark. Giant spiders now hunt through Skittering Dark and the nearby woods in western Silverpine. The abandoned mine and its approaches are dangerous to beasts and travelers alike. East of North Tide's Run, Skittering Dark lies where the western coast meets the hills. The mine once worked, but now cobwebs choke its shafts and giant spiders nest through the hollow. Krethis haunts the shadowed woods outside. The spiders hunt anything that strays too close.

subzone:skull-rock.text: Skull Rock. At Skull Rock, Burning Blade cultists gather in Durotar's eastern coastal cliffs. East of Orgrimmar, they plot against Thrall's Horde. In northeastern Durotar, Burning Blade cultists gather beneath the crags at Skull Rock. Dark cultists, fel-worshipping orcs, and summoners meet in its winding tunnels. There they practice demonic arts and plot against the young Horde. The warlock Gazz'uz leads them, and their work threatens Orgrimmar's nearby gates and travelers along the eastern shore.

subzone:sludge-fen.text:
Sludge Fen. In northeastern the Barrens, the Venture Company has turned Sludge Fen's clear pool into an oily field. Supervisor Lugwizzle oversees the drilling, while rivals in Ratchet seek to sabotage the operation. Sludge Fen once held a clear pool fed by natural springs in the arid Barrens. The Venture Company built drilling platforms and machinery over the basin. Now sludge and industrial waste fill the wetland, and crude oil is pumped around the clock.

Supervisor Lugwizzle oversees the goblin drillers, engineers, and overseers. Runoff and toxic byproducts coat the water, choking the native aquatic life beneath the grease.

subzone:solliden-farmstead.text: Solliden Farmstead. In western Tirisfal Glades, Solliden Farmstead’s human farmers still tend pumpkins north of Deathknell. Native Lordaeronians who survived the Plague of Undeath are rare in northern Lordaeron, and they cling fiercely to their soil beneath the Scarlet Crusade’s shadow. Solliden Farmstead’s fields still yield healthy crops, though much of Lordaeron lies in ruin and rot. The surviving human farmers are traumatized and keep to themselves. Scarlet Crusade patrols watch them from a nearby tower. They defend their home fiercely, striking at outsiders who come near, Horde or Alliance alike. Forsaken rising from Deathknell see Solliden Farmstead as both threat and resource. The Royal Apothecary Society wants its pristine pumpkins for testing and brewing the New Plague. So Forsaken officers such as Deathguard Simmer send fledgling recruits to raid the fields and steal pumpkins for Apothecary Johaan in Brill. They are also sent to teach the living a lesson.

subzone:south-tide-s-run.text: South Tide's Run. Along Silverpine Forest's southwestern edge, South Tide's Run meets the cold Great Sea. Its damp shore borders the forested interior and lies south of North Tide's Run. The Great Sea washes Silverpine Forest's southwestern shore. Inland, roads run east toward the Greymane Wall beneath the forest's cover. Along this open coast, the western tides meet a bleak stretch, largely untouched by inland settlements.

subzone:southern-gold-road.text:
Southern Gold Road. Caravans and travelers crowd the Southern Gold Road as it runs through the Barrens toward the Great Lift. Trade carries goods between the plains and distant reaches of Kalimdor. At the stone bridge between the northern and southern Barrens, the Southern Gold Road turns toward the Great Lift and Thousand Needles. Like the northern stretch, called the Gold Road, it takes its name from the merchant caravans that travel its length. Their trade makes the road one of Kalimdor’s busiest long-distance routes, carrying goods between remote outposts and ports.

Quilboar tribes and prowling predators harass those who travel it. Still, caravans and travelers keep moving south. Horde couriers and patrols share the Southern Gold Road with merchants and explorers bound for distant lands. Travelers journey between Gadgetzan in the deserts of Tanaris, Auberdine on the shores of Darkshore, and Nighthaven among Moonglade’s sacred groves.

For those crossing Kalimdor’s interior on foot, the sun-baked road makes for a grueling journey. Surviving the trek is a rite of passage.

subzone:spirit-rise.text:
Spirit Rise. On Thunder Bluff’s northwest mesa, Spirit Rise gathers shaman and seekers. The Skychaser tribe guides them above the Pools of Vision, where seers peer into spirit-touched waters. Spirit Rise crowns Thunder Bluff above the plains of Mulgore. Here, shaman seek communion with the elements and ancestor spirits. Rope bridges link the rise to the central mesa.

The Hall of Spirits and the Spiritual Healing pavilion draw young and veteran shaman alike. They come to deepen their bond with earth, air, fire, and water. The Skychaser tribe keeps a strong presence here and guides seekers in ancient traditions. Below the open-air totem shrines and huts, an entrance leads into the mesa. There, the steamy Pools of Vision fill a sacred cavern. Seers peer into waters touched by the spirits.

subzone:spirit-rock.text: Spirit Rock. Above the Valley of Trials in Durotar, Horde initiates climb Spirit Rock to commune with the elements. The Hidden Path winds up to the sacred crag. Spirit Rock looks down on the red canyon where young Horde warriors and scouts train. From the canyon floor, the Hidden Path winds up the rocky ridgeline to a quiet altar. There, aspiring shaman drink sapta, a traditional brew that opens their senses beyond the physical world. They listen for the earth's rumblings and whispers.

subzone:stagnant-oasis.text: Stagnant Oasis. Kolkar centaur guard the Stagnant Oasis, where wildlife gathers around its waters in the dry Barrens. The pool lies between the Gold Road and Merchant Coast. East of the Gold Road and inland from the Merchant Coast, the Stagnant Oasis breaks through the Barrens' dusty scrub. Dense foliage rings the pool, where aggressive snapjaw turtles prowl. Weakened kodos sometimes stray here from the great herds of the Field of Giants. Kolkar centaur keep camps along the banks and fiercely guard the water from anyone entering their territory. The pool looks still, yet strange life stirs beneath its surface. Deviate Fish swim among other unusual creatures. Scholars and shamans watch the Barrens oases closely. They study the strange forces that affect local springheads and the wildlife that drinks from them.

subzone:stillwater-pond.text: Stillwater Pond. Just west of Brill, Stillwater Pond lies gray and lifeless, a lost refuge for Lordaeron's children. Families from nearby hamlets once picnicked on Stillwater Pond's grassy banks. Before the Third War and the Plague of Undeath, its shallows let children too young to brave Brightwater Lake learn to swim. Now the water is gray and lifeless. The living have vanished, leaving skeletal fish below and wandering undead in the woods around it. Stillwater Pond is quieter than Tirisfal's besieged roads and contested farms, yet danger lingers along its shore. Blighted beasts drink from the murky water, including Bayne, a ferocious darkhound that stalks the banks. Travelers crossing the western meadows toward Brill must watch for predatory beasts and aimless zombies by the water's edge.

subzone:stonebull-lake.text: Stonebull Lake. At Stonebull Lake, tauren draw fresh water and fish from the heart of Mulgore. Stonebull Lake curves around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, at the heart of central Mulgore. A wooden bridge spans its narrowest stretch. The main dirt road crosses there, linking the village with Thunder Bluff on the great mesa to the north. Native fish fill the calm water. Hunters rest on the banks, travelers pause, and apprentice fishers learn their trade beneath the open sky.

subzone:the-den.text: The Den. In southwestern Durotar, young orcs and trolls gather at the sheltered Den in the heart of the Valley of Trials. It is their main base, where they train in arms and magic before setting out into the wider world. The Den is an austere proving ground, carved into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials. Inside its shadowed halls, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters answer to veterans such as Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. They receive their first combat lessons, supplies, and rites of passage, preparing for Durotar's harshness and the struggles facing the new Horde. The Den houses class trainers and merchants who provide provisions. From this field outpost, overseers send recruits to cull local beasts and aggressive quilboars. They keep a strict watch over the valley.

subzone:thorn-hill.text: Thorn Hill. At Thorn Hill, Razormane warbands strike Horde supply lines east of the Crossroads. Their fortified camp holds the high ridges between Durotar and the Barrens interior. Thorn Hill commands the roads between Durotar and the Crossroads. Razormane hunters gather here with trained wolves and geomancers who shape the earth. Elder Mystic Razorsnout guides the quilboar, and their attacks on Horde supply caravans grow bolder. So the camp, close to vital routes, is one of the Crossroads guards' most immediate threats in the central savanna.

subzone:thunder-ridge.text: Thunder Ridge. Southwest of Orgrimmar, Thunder Ridge lies along the Southfury River in western Durotar. Thunder lizards roam its stripped canyon, where human logging and dark sorcery ruined a former grove. Agitated beasts and lingering cultists threaten nearby settlements. Once, ancient trees shaded Thunder Ridge and made it a green haven in arid Durotar. Shortly after the Third War, humans from Kul Tiras began felling its timber. As the trees fell, the thunder lizards grew wild. Then the Burning Blade used fel sorcery to destroy what remained of the canopy. Now the gorge lies barren and exposed, and angry beasts that spew lightning roam its crags.

subzone:thunderhorn-water-well.text:
Thunderhorn Water Well. At Thunderhorn Water Well, tauren and their herds draw water in central Mulgore. The well lies along the path from Bloodhoof Village to Thunder Bluff, where the valley’s wells sustain life across the grasslands. The tauren must keep them clean and defended. Thunderhorn Water Well draws water from aquifers beneath central Mulgore. Nomadic tauren and settled villages alike rely on communal wells for water and sustenance. Across the plains, water is precious, and whoever controls the wells controls the land.

The Venture Company has repeatedly sought these water sources for industrial use. Their efforts threaten the balance the tribes work to preserve.

subzone:tidus-stair.text: Tidus Stair. At Tidus Stair, two tauren shamans seek insight from the coastal water spirits. The broad stone terraces rise above the Merchant Coast southeast of Ratchet, sheltered beside the Great Sea. Waves break below Tidus Stair, where weathered stone terraces climb the coastal bluffs southeast of Ratchet. The Barrens are dry and dusty, and skirmishes trouble the region, but this stretch above the Merchant Coast is quiet. A modest hut shelters Islen Waterseer and Mahren Skyseer, two tauren who live far from the goblin trade docks. They fish, watch the horizon, and seek insight from the coastal water spirits.

subzone:tiragarde-keep.text:
Tiragarde Keep. Kul Tiran marines still garrison Tiragarde Keep on Durotar’s Scuttle Coast, south of Razor Hill. Built during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s invasion, the ruined stronghold remains under Lieutenant Benedict, a hostile presence in Horde territory. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore’s fleet used Tiragarde Keep as a beachhead on Durotar’s red shores. He raised it during his campaign to destroy Thrall’s newly founded realm. The Horde broke the siege and killed Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, yet the keep was never fully abandoned.

Resupply forces under Lieutenant Benedict reclaimed its shattered stone walls. They follow the late Admiral’s standing orders to wage unyielding war against the orcs. They reject the peace Lady Jaina Proudmoore forged. White battlements rise above Durotar’s crimson cliffs, patrolled by Kul Tiran sailors and marines. The garrison raids supply lines near Razor Hill. For the Horde, the keep remains a security crisis and a proving ground.

Orc and troll commanders send young warriors to assault the fortress and cut down Benedict’s soldiers. They seek to contain the garrison before the humans push farther inland.

subzone:tor-kren-farm.text: Tor'kren Farm. At Tor'kren Farm in northwestern Durotar, Misha Tor'kren anxiously waits for news of Kron. Her son has not returned from a hunting trip. Tor'kren Farm struggles to raise pigs in Durotar's dry red dirt. The homestead lies southeast of Thunder Ridge, near the Southfury River. Feed and water run short, and nearby bluffs leave the farm isolated. Its yields are meager. Several days ago, Kron went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River. Misha Tor'kren warned him about the vicious predators, but he left in anger. Now she asks passing travelers to search for him or bring back a sign of his fate. She fears the worst, yet cannot begin mourning without knowing what happened.

subzone:trade-quarter.text: Trade Quarter. Trade Quarter draws the Undercity’s commerce and civic life beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron. Its bank, auction house, and other services serve the Forsaken capital, while corridors link it to the surrounding districts. You step from the lifts beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron into the Trade Quarter’s broad, circular halls. Canals of noxious runoff circle the central platform, crossed by bridges. The city’s coffers and bank rest there, while vendors, guild registrars, and auctioneers work along the terraces. At the inn, wooden caskets replace soft beds. Stone archways lead into the other districts, drawing the Undercity’s business through its center.

subzone:valgan-s-field.text: Valgan's Field. Worgen roam Valgan's Field above Lordamere Lake in northern Silverpine Forest. Arugal unleashed the Moonrage pack, and the Forsaken now search the ruined farm for his abandoned research. West of the Shining Strand and north of the nearby river, Valgan's Field overlooks Lordamere Lake. The wheat farm once prospered, until the Scourge swept through Lordaeron and forced Valgan to flee or die. Left untended, its buildings fell to feral Moonrage worgen prowling down from Shadowfang Keep. Before the Third War, Arugal spent time here and left remnants of his arcane research. Now the Forsaken seek them.

subzone:valley-of-honor.text: Valley of Honor. Warriors and hunters ready themselves for battle in the Valley of Honor. Its barracks, guilds, and battlemasters serve the Horde's forces across Azeroth, while forges and training grounds keep its fighters ready. The Valley of Honor holds Orgrimmar's military quarter, set behind high canyon ridges. Practice weapons clash as blacksmiths' anvils ring through the day. In the Hall of the Brave, seasoned warriors and battlemasters coordinate campaigns in places such as Alterac Valley and Warsong Gulch. Training grounds for beastmasters and hunters flank the hall. Across the valley, the Horde equips and drills its frontline defenders before sending them out. The valley supplies arms and offers a place to rest between duties. The Burning Anvil and Red Canyon Mining provide armor and raw iron. Nearby, engineers work in Nogg's Machine Shop. Grunts and visiting adventurers can fish in a quiet pool, pausing from the dust of the Valley of Strength.

subzone:valley-of-spirits.text: Valley of Spirits. In the Valley of Spirits, Darkspear trolls make their home west of Orgrimmar's main thoroughfares. Thatched lodges, tiki poles, and pools mark their place among the city's red stone and iron. The Valley of Spirits branches west from the Valley of Strength, where Darkspear trolls have made a quiet enclave. They settled in Durotar alongside Thrall's orcs and made this pocket among the crags their gathering place in the city. Around wooden bridges and winding waters, craftspeople, spiritualists, and practitioners practice their arts, away from the dry heat of Orgrimmar's main thoroughfares. The valley's lodges and pools draw those who practice magic and wild crafts. Witch doctors, herbalists, and spellcasters gather at the Spirit Lodge and Darkbriar Lodge. At the rear, the Talon Gate opens toward the Barrens' open plains, giving wanderers, hunters, and travelers a quick passage beyond the canyon walls.

subzone:valley-of-strength.text: Valley of Strength. Trade and daily business fill Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. The bank, central auction house, and Broken Tusk inn draw travelers through the Horde capital. Beyond Orgrimmar's timber gates, the Valley of Strength opens among Durotar's red canyon walls. Adventurers, merchants, and warriors from allied nations fill the Horde's front square. At the Broken Tusk inn, some trade war stories over flagons. Others turn to business at the central bank and auction house. The orcs fought for strength and unity in their new homeland, and both shape the city's heart. The Valley of Strength is Orgrimmar's foremost marketplace. Soran's Leather and Steel Armory sells armor, while vendors stock provisions for long treks across the Barrens. Grunts watch every corner. They guide newcomers and keep order among the diverse peoples who have taken refuge beneath Thrall's banner.

subzone:venomweb-vale.text:
Venomweb Vale. South of the Scarlet Monastery, Venomweb Vale lies under a swarm of venomous spiders. Once, hunters tracked deer and rabbits through its woodland. Venomweb Vale has lost its peaceful hunting ground to rot and gloom. Before the plague consumed Lordaeron, hunters followed deer and rabbits through its grass and trees. Now giant venomous spiders swarm through the trees and hollows, led by the monstrous Sri'skulk.

To the north, the Scarlet Crusade holds the neighboring territory. Darkhounds prowl near the fortified Scarlet Encampment, where Lieutenant Sanders commands.

subzone:venture-co-mine.text: Venture Co. Mine. In Mulgore’s eastern cliffs, Venture Co. Mine scars land the tauren hold sacred. The goblin company digs without permission, disturbing the plains’ natural balance. The Venture Company tunnels through Mulgore’s eastern mountain wall, though the tauren refused it mining rights. Supervisor Fizsprocket directs the work. Three entrances lead inside: a ground tunnel guarded by hired muscle, a cliffside overlook, and an upper passage to a small lumber camp. Machines, smoke, and slag heaps scar land the tauren hold sacred.

subzone:war-quarter.text: War Quarter. In the War Quarter, Lordaeron's Forsaken hone weapons and shadow magic for their fledgling kingdom. Training halls, weapon masters, and heavy industry fill the Undercity's northwest. Rank-and-file guards and elite champions drill beneath the War Quarter's gloomy stone arches. There, ruthless iron warfare meets the chilling rites of shadow. The Altar of Darkness stands at its heart. Warrior and priest guilds make the War Quarter the heart of Undercity's wartime production. Blacksmiths and smelters ring the stone with their labor as weapon masters prepare blades and armor. Iron forged deep underground arms the forces defending Lordaeron's ruins from the Scourge and Scarlet Crusade.

subzone:whispering-forest.text: Whispering Forest. Behind Deathknell, the Whispering Forest lies quiet beneath western Tirisfal’s cliffs. Its lake, giant mushroom ring, and uncanny wildlife break the stillness, while corruption stirs beneath the soil. Beyond Northface Rock and Bandarion Keep, the Whispering Forest feels far from plague-touched Tirisfal. Afflicted deer and roaming predators share its woods with a tranquil lake. Nearby, giant mushrooms form a ring beneath a hovering cloud of mist, glowing with uncanny energy. The ghostly Knight of Mourning wanders among them, bound by oath. Natural magic lingers here in land scarred by the Scourge.

subzone:whispering-shore.text: Whispering Shore. Along Tirisfal Glades' western coast, the Whispering Shore lies north of Solliden Farmstead. Hostile murlocs claim its waters. Before the Third War, Lordaeron's fishermen came to the Whispering Shore for calm water and plentiful catches. Now the Great Sea breaks against an empty coast. Its waters are cold and dark, and travelers descending from the hills risk ambush by murlocs along the shore. Hostile murlocs claim the beach and attack anyone who approaches the surf. Their chieftain, Muad, leads them as they guard the shallows and tidal flats. Nearby roads and Solliden Farmstead are under threat.

subzone:wildmane-water-well.text: Wildmane Water Well. Wildmane Water Well lies under threat as poisoned water endangers Mulgore’s northern plains and the herds that depend on it. Sacred wells sustain the tauren and their wandering kodo herds across Mulgore. Wildmane Water Well lies at the northern edge of the plains, beyond Thunder Bluff’s shadow. Venture Company goblins have poisoned its water to control the regional supply. A totem crafted by the tauren is needed to cleanse the well and make its water pure again.

subzone:windfury-ridge.text: Windfury Ridge. Windfury Ridge rises above Mulgore’s pastures, where harpies nest among wolves and cougars. Its slopes endanger travelers, and tauren hunters seek the harpies’ feathers. Windfury Ridge rises above Mulgore’s plains, its crags home to Windfury harpies. They swoop at wanderers who stray too close. Prairie wolves and mountain cougars prowl the rocky slopes, making this edge of the tauren heartland dangerous. Tauren warriors hunt the harpies for their iridescent feathers, sought in Thunder Bluff for ceremonial garments worn at feasts and weddings.

subzone:winterhoof-water-well.text: Winterhoof Water Well. Winterhoof Water Well faces a threat to Mulgore’s water supply from the Venture Company. South of Bloodhoof Village, it stands at the edge of the Rolling Plains, where tauren tribes and roaming herds depend on its fresh water. Deep wells sustain Mulgore’s herds and tauren encampments. Winterhoof Water Well draws from aquifers beneath the Rolling Plains and takes its name from one of the plains’ respected tribes. Now the Venture Company has targeted this vital source. The goblin cartel seeks control of the surrounding territory and has tried to poison the water.
